Enter the name of the service provider you want to integrate with. Example: Microsoft, Google, Zoom, SAP, etc
A client ID is used to identify the application.
A client secret is a secret key known only to the application and the authorization server. This key used to authenticate the application and obtain access tokens.
Field in the user (sys_user) table that the system uses to match the value of the subject claim in the JWT.
By default 'jti' claim in the JWT is used to verify the uniqueness of the token. If you have different claim name for uniqueness identification, update the claim name.
Provide the JWKS URL with Public key details to dynamically fetch the key during details validation.
Use this field to associate public key to this client. To associate public key, first save the record with other details and add the public key.
Add entry to JWT verifier map

Use this option to ensure that only requests using a specific, authorized token are allowed to access the API. It restricts access to API endpoints based on the authentication token, providing enhanced security by reducing the risk of unauthorized access.
Public keys once fetched using JWKS URL will be cached for 12 hours (default). In case of mismatch (key not present/key invalid) the cache will be forced refreshed.
The field lifespan is the time in seconds and represents the duration for which an access token remains valid after it is issued. Default value is: 1800 seconds (30 minutes).

Small differences in the system clocks of servers or devices involved in generating and validating a token can lead to issues when validating time-sensitive claims. Adjust the time above. Default value is: 300 seconds.
Field on sys_user to populate value in the sub claim of JWT Access Token
When you enable JTI verification, it helps prevent replay attacks by ensuring that each token is unique.
